=== Analytics reports

- Fixed an issue where exporting the *Device Utilization*, *Parallel Sessions*, and *Sessions per Day* reports as CSV or PNG returned no data. The CSV showed an export error in place of the report data.
- CSV exports of *Parallel Sessions* and *Sessions per Day* list one row per day in date order. CSV exports of *Device Utilization* sort by *Sessions*, with the most-used devices at the top.
- PNG exports of *Parallel Sessions* and *Sessions per Day* now include the report's chart as a bar chart. Previously, the PNG showed only the report title for these reports.
- Exports use the date range selected for the report, or the report's saved date range when none is selected.

=== Standalone deployment

- On Standalone deployments with GPUs, Intelligent Quality Suite (IQS) AI services now keep GPU access after system package installs, such as a GigaCap install or upgrade. Previously, these services could switch to the CPU, and IQS element finding slowed down and timed out.
- Installing or updating Standalone now stops with an error if a configured GPU ID does not match a GPU on the host. Previously, the install continued without reporting the problem.
- After you update, the IQS AI services restart once to apply the new GPU configuration.

// Source: KOB-55749 from PR #864

== Turbo Test

=== Session timeout now ends Turbo Test sessions

Turbo Test sessions now end when the session timeout (`session_timeout`) is reached. Previously, a test script that ran past the session timeout kept the session running and the device in use until the script finished on its own.

- When the session timeout is reached, Kobiton stops the test script and every process it started, ends the session, and releases the device.
- If the script does not start its session before the timeout, the run fails with a message stating that the script did not finish within the session timeout.
- Scripts that finish before the session timeout run as before.

=== Standalone deployment

- Added `sudo kobictl fix consul-server-metadata`. It repairs an unreadable Consul server metadata file that stops Consul from starting with `error reading server metadata: unexpected end of JSON input`. The fix prints the file size and contents, removes only that file, and restarts Consul. Other Consul data is kept. If the file is valid or missing, the command makes no changes.
- `sudo kobictl restart` now runs the same check automatically after each restart.

// Source: KOB-55338 from PR #868
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/868

=== Back up and restore Standalone data to a standby server

Standalone deployments can now back up Kobiton data from the primary server and restore it onto a standby server. The standby server can then take over if the primary server fails.

*Highlights*

- `sudo kobictl run backup` backs up Kobiton databases, search data, and stored files such as session videos, screenshots, and apps. Kobiton keeps running during the backup.
- Backups go to a standby server over SSH with key-based authentication, or to a locally mounted path such as a USB disk or NAS share.
- Repeat backups transfer only new or changed data.
- Backup checks free disk space before it starts. A failed backup leaves the previous complete backup intact.
- `sudo kobictl run restore <backup-path>` runs on the standby server and replaces all Kobiton data on that server with the backup. A restore can't be undone, so run it only on a standby server.
- Restore checks the Kobiton version of the standby server before it stops any services. To restore onto a standby server that runs a newer Kobiton version, add `--allow-newer`. Restore then applies the newer version's database updates.
- If a restore fails partway, Kobiton stays stopped instead of running on partially restored data. Run `sudo kobictl run restore --resume-services` to start Kobiton again.
- The license and SSL certificate aren't part of the backup. Install them on the standby server.

Replace `<backup-path>` with the path to the backup on the standby server.

*Availability*

Standalone deployments only. The standby server must run 4.27.0S or later. Backups and restores run only when started manually. Scheduled backups aren't supported.

== Passcode indicator for Android and HarmonyOS devices

The device list passcode indicator now covers Android and HarmonyOS devices, and the *Passcode* filter uses clearer labels.

- Android and HarmonyOS devices with a passcode now display the passcode icon in card view and list view, the same as iOS devices.
- The passcode icon tooltip now reads *Passcode enabled*.
- The *Passcode* filter in the device search bar now offers *Enabled* and *Not Enabled*, replacing *Supported* and *Not Supported*. *Enabled* returns devices with a passcode on every platform.

For details, see xref:devices:device-metadata.adoc#_passcode[Passcode].

=== Web views available in iOS Appium sessions

Fixed an issue where Appium automation sessions on iOS devices could intermittently return only the `NATIVE_APP` context. In affected sessions, web content opened in the app, such as a sign-in page, did not appear as a `WEBVIEW` context and could not be inspected or automated. Web views are now available as a `WEBVIEW` context in these sessions.

Web views on iOS devices still require *Web Inspector* to be turned on in *Settings → Safari → Advanced*.

- Fixed an issue where *Appium Inspector* in Session Explorer showed the same XML hierarchy for every step of an iPad automation session started without an app, such as a web session in Safari. *Appium Inspector* now shows the hierarchy for each step of these sessions, as it already does on iPhone and Android devices. iPad automation sessions that install an app, and manual sessions on iPad, are unchanged.
